behavioral_effects: A host dedicated to Codecov can deploy Traefik plus Codecov without the application stack, its external volumes, or the GPU services
The Linux deployment command is written down once, in MANUAL_STEPS, matching the recipe verbatim
compatibility_impact: prod-codecov no longer requires make prod to have run; on a host that did run make prod, starting traefik again is a no-op because it is already up. No compose, image, or contract change.
limitations: The documented Linux command has been validated by compose-check only; the first real run against a Linux host is the deployment that follows this change and its result belongs in the next record
preflight-codecov stays PowerShell-only by the repository's own rule; a Linux operator gets no placeholder guard beyond the doc's instruction to check the file
reason: prod-codecov assumes make prod already started Traefik and reaches its Compose command only through a PowerShell preflight, so on a Linux host dedicated to Codecov — where the application stack, its GPU services, and powershell.exe do not exist — the target fails before Docker is touched and Traefik is never started; starting Traefik from the target itself and recording the raw Compose command as the Linux path lets a Codecov-only host deploy without the application
rollback: git revert. Nothing outside the repository is affected.
security_impact: None. prod-codecov starts Traefik plus the Codecov services; the set of published ports is unchanged (Traefik 80/443, dashboard loopback-only, nothing from codecov-gateway). The Linux-host path documented in MANUAL_STEPS bypasses the PowerShell placeholder guard, and the doc says so explicitly and tells the operator to check backend/.env themselves.
summary: Make prod-codecov deploy standalone with Traefik and document the Linux host command
